title: Australia Bans AI-Made Songs from Music Charts
paragraphs: AI can now create songs, vocals and instruments. But should a song made entirely by AI be able to enter the same music charts as songs made by real people?
The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA), which runs the country's official music charts, says "No!"
ARIA has announced that songs must now be mostly made by humans to be able to enter its charts. AI can still be used as a tool, but it can't create most or all of the music.

The change comes at an interesting time for Josh Fawaz, an Australian DJ and music producer, as his version of Madonna's "Like a Prayer" has become one of the most-played songs on Australian radio. The song has also been at the top of ARIA's Australian Dance Singles chart for several weeks, and has about 50 million Spotify streams.
But as the song has become popular, many people have begun to claim Fawaz used AI to help make it. And music producer Mitch Thomas even said on social media that Fawaz's song was made entirely by AI.
Explaining to ABC News why he has a problem with AI-made music, Thomas said, "It just kind of feels like cheating."
Fawaz, however, says he only used AI "as a tool." But since it was first released, the song's Spotify credits have been changed to show that AI was used for its vocals and drums.

ARIA CEO Annabelle Herd said the new rules aren't there to stop artists from using AI. Artists can keep using the technology to help them make music, but humans should still do most of the creative work.
For now, ARIA hasn't said whether Fawaz's song will remain on its charts or not.
